Theo: Hey legal/ops — we're bringing up a model called Crown-13B from an external repo. License PDF linked: https://example.com/crown-13b-license. Quick read: it has a clause that seems to forbid 'commercial hosting' and also mentions 'no redistribution of weights'. Can we host this (hosted API) if we quantize to q4 and only serve tokens?
Maya: we ran a quick q4_v2 conversion, perf is good (latency and cost win). technically we only plan to serve via API, not hand out weights. sample run: 
```bash
python eval.py --model crown-13b --quant q4_v2 --batch 8
```
But if the upstream forbids hosting, that could block Hosted offering.
Liz: Thanks. Short answer: it depends on exact wording. Paste the clause here if you can. If it literally forbids 'providing a hosted service' that's an explicit ban on hosting. If it's only about redistribution, serving via an API can still be considered hosting in many licenses.
Theo: here's the exact excerpt from the license doc: "The model weights, in any form (including quantized or converted derivatives), may not be redistributed, sublicensed, or used to provide a hosted service for commercial purposes without an express commercial license from the rights holder."
Liz: That's quite explicit. Two parts to parse: (1) redistributing weights (includes quantized derivatives) is banned, and (2) using the model to provide a hosted service for commercial purposes is also banned unless we obtain an express commercial license.
Sam: So Hosted API for paying customers is out unless we get a commercial license. What about Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Private (VPC/on-prem)?
Liz: Private (customer-managed deployment or on-prem) is safest: since the customer runs the model themselves, Redwood isn't 'providing a hosted service' in the upstream's sense. For Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved GPU pools) it's still us running the service, so that would count as hosting.
Maya: clarifying: if a customer buys Dedicated capacity and we spin up the model in their dedicated pool but we still manage the infra, is that considered "we're providing a hosted service"?
Liz: Yes — management + serving by Redwood counts as providing the hosted service under the clause. The boundary is who controls and is responsible for serving. If the customer self-hosts in their own VPC with their license, that's OK.
Theo: What about caching/kv caches or transient memory like sharded checkpoints we keep for performance? Is that redistribution?
Liz: Short: transient in-memory caches used only to serve requests are less likely to be viewed as redistribution. But persistent storage of the model artifacts in a place where third parties can access them is redistribution. Quantized artifacts are explicitly called out in the clause you pasted, so generating and shipping quantized files to customers would definitely be redistribution.
Maya: ok — so plan: block Crown-13B from Hosted, block from Redwood-managed Dedicated, allow as Private only if customer brings license and we verify rights. We'll also avoid exporting quantized files to anyone.
Sam: we should add a short note to the onboarding checklist so solutions/sales don't accidentally promise Hosted. Also we need a commercial license request template to send upstream.
Liz: I'll draft a short template. For now: mark model status = "blocked-hosted" in onboarding tracker and add a remediation item: "obtain express commercial license to enable hosted/dedicated".
ops-bot: Ticket created: ENGML-8342 — "Crown-13B licensing: hosting/redistribution clarification and commercial license request" (assignee: Theo)
Theo: thanks. I'll update the model registry entry and change the eval runs to a private-only flag so we don't accidentally surface results in public docs.
Maya: will update our CI to not publish weight artifacts and to skip packaging quant files. I'll also run a side-by-side eval against allowed models and post numbers here once done.
Liz: one more note: if upstream later grants a commercial license, ensure we capture the exact rights in the contract: hosting, redistribution of derivatives, sublicensing etc. If they only allow "hosting but not redistribution", we still can't hand out quantized files.
Theo: got it. tagging for follow-up: @Liz @Sam @Maya. Thanks everyone.
